correctness.rationale: Equation (5) is obtained by a forest-block incidence Gram determinant and Kirchhoff. Pair counting by ordered component partitions, internal Cayley trees and the weighted Cayley identity gives (1) with exact factors n! n^(r-n)/r!. Coefficients of e^-s s^(s-1/2)/s! are c/s+O(s^-2); L(z)^r has leading r log(n)^(r-1)/n; all remainder terms are lower logarithmic order, yielding the normalized constant (2). Rectangular sublinear component ranges and the exact conditioned product law prove the annealed r-1 uniform logarithmic limits, without a uniform-edge-cut claim. The independent exact checker passed 294278 forest-subset observations (all trees n<=6 and n=7 at r=3), with exact Gram determinants for n<=6; finite tests are not treated as proofs for arbitrary n.

originality.rationale: The identified contribution is the geometric Cayley-tree all-codimension expectation and the induced critical logarithmic size hierarchy, not the classical zonotope minor identity, multivariate Cayley identity or Gibbs/Kolchin theory. Full primary material from graphical-zonotope, i.i.d. random-zonotope, general Gibbs and random-tree uncover work does not present this combined geometric statement. The r=2 surface expectation was already available and is explicitly outside the new range. Residual equivalent Gibbs-assembly specializations remain possible.
residual_risks: Known abstract logarithmic Gibbs-partition theorems may imply part of the size law once the geometric weight is identified; no independent novelty is claimed for general Gibbs theory.
Uninspected equivalent applications in older random-tree forestry or stochastic-geometry literature may exist despite targeted searches; bibliographic novelty is assessed with stated limits.
No independent mathematical audit has been performed.

value.rationale: All tree graphical zonotopes have the same full intrinsic Euclidean volume and combinatorial parallelotope type, yet their higher intrinsic volumes vary. The exact all-fixed-codimension Cayley expectation, sharp n^(r-1/2) log(n)^(r-1) scale and the geometry-induced one-giant/multiple-log-uniform law identify a natural structural interaction between Euclidean minors, graph forests and logarithmic partitions. The precise all-r formula and size law go beyond the known one-cut surface expectation and motivated finite table lookups.
